Gradient training fits overparameterized networks

Under suitable conditions, gradient training can bring large networks near zero training classification error. Zhang et al., 2016 ↗

Optimization

In brief

Gradient training can drive large convolutional networks to zero or near-zero training error, even with random labels. Independent groups reproduce this on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Success depends on architecture, initialization and training recipe: smaller models and early stopping leave substantial training error. Batch normalization can speed training and shortcut connections can help deep networks train, but whether these benefits hold generally is contested. Fitting the training data well need not improve performance on unseen data.

Papers to start with: Zhang et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2018; Safran et al., 2018

Success depends on architecture, initialization and training recipe; smaller models, early stopping and some regularized recipes leave substantial training error.
Original resultZhang et al., 2016 ↗

Zhang et al. trained Inception and Alexnet with SGD on CIFAR-10 using true, partially corrupted and random labels.

Inception and Alexnet reached 100.0% training accuracy on true and random labels without random cropping or weight decay, and Inception perfectly fit every tested partial-corruption level. Alexnet failed to converge on random labels with default weight decay.

                Extra capacity changes access to useful solutions 38 studies

                Extra width or effective capacity changes convergence reliability, specialization and recovery. Benefits depend on target geometry, activation and training method.

                  Representable targets can remain difficult to learn 32 studies

                  Realizability and extra width do not universally remove suboptimal minima, slow stationary regions or obstacles to feature recovery.

                    Favorable landscapes do not establish training success 31 studies

                    Width, rank and connectivity can improve critical-point geometry or connectivity between low-loss solutions under stated assumptions. These results do not establish ordinary training success.

                      Original resultHe et al., 2016 ↗

                      He et al. compared plain and identity-shortcut convolutional networks with batch normalization on ImageNet and CIFAR-10.

                      On ImageNet, the 34-layer plain network had higher training error than the 18-layer plain network throughout training, while the 34-layer ResNet outperformed the 18-layer ResNet and 34-layer plain network. On CIFAR-10, plain-110 exceeded 60% training error, while ResNet-1202 achieved below 0.1%.

                                V4Initialization controls training speed and trainable depth 76310 Suggested status R2independently reproducedSeveral independent groups reproduce the findings that initialization affects whether training succeeds and that, under some conditions, orthogonal weights train deep tanh networks faster than Gaussian weights. Orthogonal and Gaussian training dynamics become nearly equal in wide networks at small learning rates in the neural tangent kernel regime, where a linear approximation around the initial parameters describes training; the 10,000-layer CNN demonstration remains an original-study result.
                                Original resultXiao et al., 2018 ↗

                                Xiao et al. compared orthogonal and equal-variance Gaussian initialization and tested Delta-Orthogonal CNNs on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

                                A 4,000-layer orthogonally initialized CNN reached 95% accuracy on MNIST after 10,000 steps, while Gaussian initialization stayed below 60% training and test accuracy after 90,000 steps. The study also reported training and test curves for Delta-Orthogonal CNNs up to 10,000 layers, without numerical training accuracy in the text.

                                        Related findings5 groups of studies

                                        Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

                                        Useful learning rates depend on training conditions 94 studies

                                        Useful learning rates, warmup and decay timing depend on optimizer, depth, initialization, batch size and training phase.

                                          Stability diagnostics must reflect the actual updates 56 studies

                                          Stability depends on optimizer state, stochastic curvature, eigenspaces and the directions and relative sizes of parameter updates. Sharpness measured using the Hessian over the full training set is not a universal diagnostic.

                                            Training can recover from temporary loss growth 25 studies

                                            Training can recover after temporary increases in loss, even beyond squared-loss networks. The mechanisms depend on the objective, noise, initialization and schedule.

                                              Stable loss can coexist with moving parameters 20 studies

                                              Decreasing or stabilized loss can coexist with bounded oscillations, cycles, chaos or nonconvergent parameter trajectories.

                                                Large steps require more than local stability 7 studies

                                                Large-step convergence and escape depend on objective, separability, data geometry and schedule. Local stability alone does not ensure global convergence.

                                                  Training choices and constraints

                                                  Update rules, parameterization, numerical choices and specialized training requirements affect successful fitting, efficiency and continued adaptation.

                                                  Alternative training methods change outcomes and costs 77 studies

                                                  Alternative training spaces, updates and optimizers change convergence, failure modes and predictive performance. Their computational tradeoffs depend on the task.

                                                    Noise and batching change optimization behavior 20 studies

                                                    Noise structure, sampling and batch size change escape, loss regimes and implicit regularization. Tuned deterministic recipes reproduce some SGD outcomes.

                                                      Sparse training depends on connectivity and budget 20 studies

                                                      Sparse-network training and recovery depend on masks, surviving initialization, connectivity, pruning severity and training budget.

                                                        Parameterization can support transfer across scale 14 studies

                                                        Parameterizations that account for width, depth and sparsity can stabilize feature updates and hyperparameter transfer. Their effectiveness remains dependent on the training recipe.

                                                          Maintained weight constraints affect training 13 studies

                                                          Maintaining orthogonal, norm and zero-sum constraints changes optimization beyond initialization alone. Outcomes depend on the constraint and architecture.

                                                            Numerical choices affect fitting and efficiency 12 studies

                                                            Numerical precision, quantization and rescaling affect gradients, fitting and efficiency. Their effects depend on format, architecture and normalization.

                                                              Training history can impair later adaptation 9 studies

                                                              Training history and changing targets can impair subsequent fitting. Norm control, regularization and suitable architecture or learning-rate interventions can preserve adaptation.

                                                                Spiking-network training depends on dynamics and signal paths 9 studies

                                                                Neuron dynamics, surrogate gradients, temporal regularization and signal-path design condition direct spiking-network training.

                                                                  Quantum gradient diagnostics do not certify trainability 8 studies

                                                                  Quantum initialization, output scaling and circuit structure change gradients and fitting. Favorable gradient diagnostics do not certify optimization success.

                                                                    Interpreting training dynamics

                                                                    Feature evolution and solution selection help explain training trajectories, while simplified models apply only within particular regimes.

                                                                    Optimization biases which fitting solutions emerge 61 studies

                                                                    Initialization, parameterization and optimizer dynamics bias the sparsity, rank, alignment, norms and functions of learned solutions.

                                                                      Fixed kernels describe only some training regimes 45 studies

                                                                      Width, scaling and training determine feature evolution and agreement with linearized models. Fixed-kernel descriptions have limits that depend on the task and training regime.

                                                                        Training surrogates have limited validity 13 studies

                                                                        Continuous-time and local surrogate models describe selected discrete training regimes. Step size, noise, nonlinear dynamics and optimizer state limit their validity.

                                                                          Evaluating generalization and robustness

                                                                          Evaluate held-out performance, robustness and delayed generalization separately from training fit, speed and sharpness.

                                                                          Initialization changes held-out performance 52 studies

                                                                          Initialization and activation choices change held-out performance. Their rankings depend on the task and need not track fitting speed.

                                                                            Better training fits need not improve generalization 46 studies

                                                                            Perfect fits, lower training loss and faster fitting need not improve held-out, minority-group or adversarial performance.

                                                                              Normalization changes final predictive performance 44 studies

                                                                              Normalization changes final predictive performance. Method rankings depend on architecture, task, batch size, regularization and arithmetic.

                                                                                Lower sharpness alone does not establish improvement 39 studies

                                                                                Sharpness changes and their associations with generalization depend on measurement, parameterization and training recipe. Lower sharpness alone does not establish better learning or generalization.

                                                                                  Training choices change perturbation robustness 16 studies

                                                                                  Training and normalization interventions change perturbation robustness. Tradeoffs with clean performance and convergence depend on architecture.

                                                                                      Where to start reading

                                                                                      1. 1

                                                                                        Chiyuan Zhang et al., 2016 ↗ Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization

                                                                                        Establishes SGD fitting of true and random labels, with cropping and weight decay disabled for random labels.

                                                                                      2. 2

                                                                                        Quynh Nguyen et al., 2018 ↗ On the loss landscape of a class of deep neural networks with no bad local valleys

                                                                                        Sigmoid VGG fitting depends on layer-skipping connections to the output and training duration, qualifying claims that any architecture fits.

                                                                                      3. 3

                                                                                        Itay Safran et al., 2018 ↗ Spurious Local Minima are Common in Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks

                                                                                        Demonstrates frequent suboptimal local minima in realizable two-layer ReLU networks under expected squared-loss gradient descent and Xavier initialization.

                                                                                      Known gaps in this draft

                                                                                      Unexplained convergence discrepancies, an omitted initialization comparison, unclear support for kernel qualifications and unresolved questions about factual accuracy limit confidence in the conclusions.

                                                                                      All 6 gaps
                                                                                      • Reported global convergence at teacher width 17 and student width 19 differs between tables: 99.63% versus 77.50%. The reason for this discrepancy remains unexplained.
                                                                                      • Initialization evidence remains incomplete without the comparison showing unsuccessful small-variance Gaussian initialization and successful Kaiming initialization in plain convolutional networks on MNIST and STL10. Its different training recipe limits direct comparison with other initialization results.
                                                                                      • The qualification concerning neural tangent kernel descriptions needs explicit supporting results that readers can assess directly.
                                                                                      • Several findings still have unresolved extraction or source discrepancies. Their factual reliability remains uncertain.
                                                                                      • Evidence checks identified factual errors and incorrect interpretations. It remains unclear whether every affected conclusion was corrected or excluded.
                                                                                      • Of 310 selected source checks, 305 were full reads; four remain partial and one has mismatched source text. Those five are not fully verified.
